description: This case study is the National Transportation Safety Board's pipeline accident report on the overpressurization of the natural gas distribution system in the Merrimack Valley of Massachusetts on 13 September 2018, adopted on 24 September 2019 as NTSB/PAR-19/02. Around 4:00 p.m. high-pressure gas was released into a low-pressure system owned by Columbia Gas of Massachusetts, a NiSource subsidiary serving about 325,000 customers, starting a series of structure fires and explosions in Lawrence, Andover and North Andover. One person died, 22 people were taken to hospital, 131 structures were damaged, fire departments used the state mobilisation plan with mutual aid from New Hampshire and Maine, electric power was cut in the area, and the gas system was shut down for 10,894 customers. Access: free PDF download from the NTSB; no licence is stated. Coverage is one event in three towns. Caveats: only the abstract and front matter of the 74-page report were read here, and the cause and finding sections were not summarised. It suits emergency response and resilience studies of gas distribution systems, and it relates to the NTSB investigation page record catalogued here as case_study-ntsb-merrimack-valley-gas-overpressurization-2018.

outcomes: High-pressure gas released into a low-pressure distribution system started fires and explosions that killed one person, injured 22 people transported to hospitals and seven firefighters, and damaged 131 structures including at least five destroyed homes. The system was shut down for 10,894 customers, and the NTSB made recommendations to the pipeline safety regulator, the 34 states with an industrial exemption for gas infrastructure projects, Massachusetts public safety officials and NiSource.
